agent_2.name: Lucas
agent_2.occupation: software engineer and boyfriend of Sophia

metadata.scenario_context: Sophia has been promoted to the position of a Team Manager at her workplace, and her friends are throwing her a surprise party to celebrate her accomplishment.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message: Lucas, what do you think about giving Sophia yellow flowers for her promotion? They symbolize happiness and success, perfect for the occasion.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: Yellow flowers sound like a great idea, but I was thinking maybe something more traditional, like orchids, which are very symbolic in Taiwanese culture, you know, to show respect and wishes for her continued success, that would make my parents proud.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message: Orchids are nice, but I'm not sure that's the point. I mean, we want to celebrate Sophia's achievement, not just make our parents proud. Speaking of which, do you strongly agree that one of your main goals in life has been to make your parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: Yes, I do strongly agree with that. Making my parents proud is very important to me, it's a big part of my values. And I think giving Sophia a thoughtful gift that reflects my heritage will actually make them proud, and that's a nice bonus to celebrating her success.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message: I see it differently. I don't think making our parents proud should be a main goal. It's Sophia's day, let's focus on her. Yellow flowers are still a great idea, don't you think? And by the way, do you really think making your parents proud is that important to you, or is it just something you've been told is important?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: I understand where you're coming from, but for me, making my parents proud is not just something I've been told, it's genuinely important. And I think a thoughtful gift, like orchids, shows I'm considering my roots and my family, which is important to me, and that's not going to change.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message: I still disagree, but let's not argue about it. The party is about Sophia, after all. So, are we going with the yellow flowers or the orchids? And by the way, I still don't think making parents proud should be a top priority...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out, and with experience you can handle any situation. Doesn't matter to me, let's just focus on getting a nice gift for Sophia. How about we combine both ideas, get some yellow orchids or something? Live and let live, right?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mark
turns.message: Yellow orchids, that's a compromise I can live with. But just to clarify, I still don't think making my parents proud is a main goal for me, and I don't see why it should be. Anyway, let's get those yellow orchids and make Sophia happy. GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Acceptance
